question.text: Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund (Cat III) breached its permitted leverage limit on a Monday due to an overnight FX move. The custodian's reporting obligation to SEBI is to report:

answer.text: Within 30 days along with the quarterly NAV report.
Before 10 a.m. on the next working day, providing the fund name, extent of breach and reasons.
Only if the breach lasts more than 5 consecutive trading days.
Annually, as part of the PPM audit.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9.7.2 states: 'In the case of Category III AIFs with a breach of their permitted leverage limits, the custodian shall report to SEBI providing name of the fund, the extent of breach and reasons for the same before 10 a.m. on the next working day.' The Trap: Option A under-reports (the urgency is same-day/next-morning). Option C invents a grace period. Option D conflates with the annual audit. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same reporting-window. XIX-B (Distributor) may ask how clients learn of a breach — typically via the subsequent disclosure, not the next-morning SEBI report. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build a pre-market leverage dashboard for your Cat III — flag any breach by 8 a.m. IST so you have a 2-hour buffer to coordinate with the custodian's SEBI filing by 10 a.m. and simultaneously execute de-risk trades at market open.
